examQuestions.question: State the portable naming subset used in this course and explain case sensitivity.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Begin with a letter and continue with letters, digits or internal underscores; avoid leading underscores as a conservative convention. A digit cannot start a name and keywords cannot be reused. score and Score are different C identifiers.

examQuestions.question: Explain identifier legality, reserved-name rules and a naming convention suitable for marks-report code.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
Use meaningful snake_case names such as theory_marks and remaining_balance. Names beginning with underscore followed by uppercase or another underscore are reserved for any use, and leading underscores have additional file-scope reservations. Library names have further restrictions, so absence from the keyword list is insufficient proof of availability. Digits may follow the first letter, but spaces and hyphens split tokens. Include units when they prevent ambiguity and avoid names distinguished only by case.

Marking: spelling 1, reserved patterns 2, convention and examples 2.

examQuestions.question: Write a complete C program for this lab task: Read item_count and unit_price each 0 to 100; print Input: then subtotal=S and with_fee=F on separate lines, F=S+5.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int item_count, unit_price;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%d %d", &item_count, &unit_price) != 2) {
        return 1;
    }
    int subtotal = item_count * unit_price;
    printf("subtotal=%d\nwith_fee=%d\n", subtotal, subtotal + 5);
    return 0;
}

Marking: 1 for typed declarations, 1 for checked input, 2 for the required calculation or transformation, and 1 for exact output.
